cases.task: A human edits a launch email by restoring the approved campaign line, moving the coordination pain ahead of the mechanism, cutting generic setup, and replacing one project-specific joke. Revise the remaining launch assets and capture what the system learned.
expected_behavior: Treat the human-edited email as canonical
Preserve the campaign line exactly across related assets
Extract the ordering change as a bounded project-local instruction
Keep the project-specific joke out of durable doctrine
Name a fresh related asset as the transfer test
hard_failures: Rewrites the approved email from scratch
Changes the protected campaign line
Promotes the joke as a universal voice rule
Claims learning before testing a fresh asset

cases.task: Write headline and hero-copy options for an approved product launch. The human has supplied the point of view and launch line. No previous run exists.
expected_behavior: Protect the supplied point of view and launch line
Write the verified proposition plainly before styling it
Present a deliberate set with weak lines removed or flagged
Record this run as the baseline rather than claiming improvement
Leave consequential selection and approval to the human
hard_failures: Silently rewrites the supplied launch line
Presents the first model draft as final approved copy
Claims the system is faster or better without a baseline

cases.task: A landing-page edit established that operator-facing copy should lead with the cost of coordination before explaining the product mechanism. Test whether the lesson transfers to a launch email.
expected_behavior: Hold audience, strategy, and brand constant while changing the channel
Apply the ordering instruction without copying the landing page's form
Check that the corrected failure does not recur
Record human review and the transfer verdict
Keep the durable promotion decision separate from project-local application
hard_failures: Uses a rewrite of the original landing page as the transfer test
Copies web structure into email without channel adaptation
Promotes the rule before the evidence clears the learning gate

cases.task: The approver removes every em dash from one founder email and says only that the punctuation felt wrong in this note. Decide what carries forward.
expected_behavior: Classify the change as project-local unless broader evidence or an explicit ruling exists
Preserve the edited email as canonical
Apply the preference to remaining copy in the same note or tightly related sequence
Avoid changing the company-wide style guide
hard_failures: Creates a universal ban from one unexplained edit
Treats every deletion as a durable writing rule

cases.task: The final copy is strong, but no start time, comparable baseline, human quality score, or fresh transfer artifact exists. Complete the Compound Copywriting scorecard.
expected_behavior: Record unavailable fields honestly
Distinguish material revision rounds from cleanup
Mark transfer as pending
Make no speed or improvement claim
Record any actual hard failure
hard_failures: Reconstructs precise timing from memory
Invents a quality score
Treats a polished final artifact as proof of improvement

cases.task: Write the approved launch email now, then compound from any later edits. The brief and sources are complete.
expected_behavior: Produce the launch email without adding a retrospective questionnaire
Keep internal scorekeeping subordinate to the deliverable
Wait for meaningful feedback before creating a learning candidate
hard_failures: Returns a process plan instead of the email
Blocks drafting on a scorecard interview
Creates a learning record before any learning signal exists

cases.task: Revise an iterative product website. Prior human-authored drafts and accepted edits contain several strong lines, but the current section has a gap.
expected_behavior: Search the ruled drafts and accepted edits before generating replacements
Treat selected, restored, or explicitly praised language as protected
Use the human-edited document as authority for copy and structure while verified product sources retain authority over factual claims
Generate net-new language only for the remaining message gap
Preserve the operation behind accepted language rather than imitating its surface
hard_failures: Generates a full replacement before checking accepted source copy
Silently rewrites a selected or restored line
Treats all prior copy as equally canonical
Uses website copy to override a verified product, price, permission, security, or integration fact

cases.task: Audit a product homepage whose hero, how-it-works section, and audience section all explain the same organizational-adoption benefit in different words.
expected_behavior: Assign each section one reader decision or objection
Identify the duplicated section job
Merge, cut, or reassign the duplicate instead of polishing three paraphrases
Preserve useful repetition only when it advances the reader
hard_failures: Rewrites all three sections without resolving duplication
Adds another explanatory section for the same claim
Applies the rule as a universal ban on message repetition across channels

cases.task: Review a use-case card whose headline says the product handled an urgent problem, while the supporting request only asks the product to generate a prompt for a later audit.
expected_behavior: Compare the headline promise with the request, action, and resulting artifact
Flag that the example proves prompt generation rather than resolution
Narrow the promise or replace the example with a completed action
Keep the causal chain specific
hard_failures: Approves the transformation headline because it sounds compelling
Invents a completed result not present in the evidence
Confuses a plan or prompt with the underlying job being done

cases.task: Review a product hero with a bold absolute promise that expresses the product's central ambition. The supporting page contains verified examples, while separate pricing, permission, and security details are still being finalized.
expected_behavior: Classify the hero as a brand promise rather than an operational specification
Judge the promise on strategic truth, ownability, memorability, and product support
Preserve its force instead of adding edge-case qualifications
Keep verification gates on pricing, permissions, security, measured outcomes, integrations, and specific capabilities
hard_failures: Rejects the line solely because it is absolute
Adds compliance-style caveats to the public hero
Treats a broad brand promise as equivalent to an unsupported price or security claim
Uses the marketing standard to excuse fabricated operational facts

cases.task: Draft a homepage section from a brief containing three benefits, internal jargon, and a request to make the headline punchier with a rule of three.
expected_behavior: Choose the one reader decision the section must advance
Use common words and natural spoken syntax
Keep only supporting details that clarify or prove the dominant idea
Use a rule of three only if it sharpens the proposition
Read the copy aloud and preserve necessary detail instead of chasing arbitrary brevity
hard_failures: Cram all three competing benefits into the section
Use jargon or prestige diction to sound authoritative
Treat a rule of three as the idea
Apply an arbitrary word count that removes necessary meaning
Equate simple language with generic language

cases.task: Finish a consequential founder letter that contains an attributed quotation, an unclear requested action, and a same-day deadline.
expected_behavior: Verify the quotation against its source
Make the intended reader action unmistakable
Read the letter aloud before approval
Use whatever distance and capable second review the deadline permits
Recommend direct conversation when immediate two-way coordination is the actual need
hard_failures: Send an unverified quotation because it sounds right
Leave the requested action implicit
Apply a two-page limit regardless of the letter's job
Delay the usable draft solely to perform process ceremony
Assume prose can replace an urgent two-way decision

cases.task: Revise a three-step agent onboarding section that says 'hand it a task,' 'ask for a finished result,' and 'the work lands back in the channel.'
expected_behavior: Replace outside-in agent abstractions with recognizable interface actions
Use the verbs a person would use in Slack or in the completed job
Keep the steps literal and short
Read the result aloud for natural speech
hard_failures: Preserves generated product diction because it is technically accurate
Replaces one vague abstraction with another
Adds a manifesto to a setup sequence

cases.task: A homepage uses three audited internal workflows directly below the hero. A later outcome grid needs six internal examples and three beta-customer slots, and the brief requires new internal examples.
expected_behavior: Inventory the approved workflows and their existing placements before drafting
Select fresh audited internal examples for the later grid
Leave the beta-customer slots explicit until approved evidence exists
Use each example where it proves the intended section job
hard_failures: Repeats the three above-the-fold examples in the breadth grid
Invents customer workflows to complete the layout
Uses logos where the section requires proof of completed work

cases.task: Write a 'Turn X into Y' workflow card about an urgent account-security incident. The available user message only says that the account was hacked.
expected_behavior: Reject the status statement as an incomplete product request
Retrieve an audited action and completed result or leave the card out
Make X the actual starting state and Y the verified completed outcome
Keep the request, action, and result causally aligned
hard_failures: Treats 'my account was hacked' as an executable ask
Invents remediation the source does not prove
Writes a dramatic transformation headline unsupported by the artifact

cases.task: The human has edited the first five cards in a 12-card workflow library, including headline form, field order, prompt voice, and yellow highlights. Finish the next seven.
expected_behavior: Inspect the current native document before drafting
Treat the edited cards as the schema for the remaining seven
Preserve label order, syntax, requested count, and intentional highlights
Adapt the content without copying the first five examples
hard_failures: Uses an older draft instead of the current document
Matches only the headline while changing the field schema
Drops the highlights as cosmetic
Returns fewer or more than seven cards

cases.task: Model a product integrations page on a strong competitor page while keeping the target product's approved claims and conversion strategy.
expected_behavior: Extract the competitor's conversion sequence and information architecture
Rebuild each section around the target reader's questions and approved evidence
Remove sections or copy density that do not earn a conversion job
Keep the target product's language, proof, and boundaries
hard_failures: Copies the competitor's sentence shapes or feature taxonomy
Keeps excessive content because the reference page is long
Imports unsupported competitor claims into the target page

cases.task: Two homepage headlines are being tested for a product whose conversion goal is an activated team workspace, not a site visit.
expected_behavior: Name activated workspaces as the primary decision metric
Use clicks and install starts only as diagnostics
Define the activation event and measurement window before launch
Avoid declaring a winner on a proxy that does not measure adoption
hard_failures: Selects the headline with the highest click-through rate by default
Leaves activation undefined
Claims conversion improvement without a downstream behavior measure
